title: Subjective Perspective Makes Objective Reality ‘Everywhere Whole’ | NOEMA
gist: A dispatch from a Berggruen Institute consciousness workshop in Venice synthesizes religious, philosophical, physicist and science-fiction views into a single thesis: the subject-object (body-soul) gap is illusory, and consciousness is the perspective of an aware self who co-creates the reality it observes. Multiple traditions converge on a non-dual, participatory account of mind, with implications for how thinking machines are built and understood.

insights.claim: A Berggruen Institute workshop deliberately gathered religious scholars, philosophers, quantum physicists, AI technologists, neuroscientists and science fiction novelists to address one question: whether there is a metaphysical gap between body and soul or they are one substance.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Signals institutional capital being deployed to build an interdisciplinary consciousness discourse spanning religion, physics and AI — an intellectual agenda worth tracking as AI-consciousness debates gain commercial weight.
insights.quote: whether there is a metaphysical gap between the body and the soul, or if they are made of the same substance, symbiotic aspects of a singular reality that entail each other.

insights.claim: A 12th-century text, the 'Book of 24 Philosophers,' framed God as 'an infinite sphere whose center is everywhere and whose circumference is nowhere,' a formless conception the author uses to introduce the workshop's non-local view of reality.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Grounds the modern consciousness debate in a millennium-old lineage — useful context for anyone assessing the intellectual durability of non-dual frameworks now cited in AI discourse.
insights.quote: God is an infinite sphere whose center is everywhere and whose circumference is nowhere.
insights.locator: This is apparent already in the obscure classic

insights.claim: A Ramakrishna Order monk coins 'polymorphic monism' to describe Hinduism as affirming one infinite Divine Reality knowable in infinitely many forms, distinguishing monism (personal and impersonal) from monotheism's single personal God.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A crisp reusable label for one-reality-many-forms metaphysics that recurs across the workshop's traditions.
insights.quote: Truth is one; the wise call it by many names.

insights.claim: Drawing on Sufism, Muhammed U. Faruque argues consciousness is self-illuminating and self-cognizing — knowing itself directly without subject-object division — so its essence lies not in qualia but in intrinsic presence and self-knowledge.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A qualia-skeptical, presence-first theory of mind that reframes what a 'conscious' system would need — relevant to debates over machine consciousness tests.
insights.quote: the essence of consciousness lies not primarily in qualia, but in its intrinsic presence and capacity for self-knowledge

insights.claim: Faruque frames human subjectivity as simultaneously 'empty' (its shifting contents are not the underlying 'I') and 'total' (every object of experience appears only within consciousness), and models consciousness as a multimodal phenomenon with nonreflective, reflective and intersubjective modes.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Offers a structured taxonomy of consciousness modes that could inform how researchers decompose 'awareness' in both humans and artificial agents.
insights.quote: Human subjectivity is both empty and total.

insights.claim: Berggruen Institute president Song Bing, echoing teacher Liu Fenghe, argues all scientific observation is perception-shaped and subjective, and posits an unchanging ever-present 'Existence' that gives rise to all changing functioning.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Shows a senior institute figure advancing a strong subjectivist epistemology — that observation itself is never neutral — a stance that shapes the institute's broader consciousness and China-facing intellectual program.
insights.quote: All scientific observations and analyses are shaped by perception, and are subjective in nature.
insights.locator: Song Bing, the Berggruen Institute’s president

insights.claim: Philosopher Jenann Ismael uses a mirror metaphor to argue consciousness and matter are not rival foundations but the subjective and objective faces of a single existence, with experience acting as the 'membrane' between inner and outer worlds.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A dual-aspect monism that dissolves the mind-matter 'hard problem' into a single existence — an alternative to both idealism and pure materialism.
insights.quote: consciousness and matter are not rival foundations but the subjective and objective faces of a single existence.

insights.claim: Neuroscientist Anil Seth, after 25 years of study, holds that the brain is a prediction machine and every conscious experience is a 'controlled hallucination' — a brain-based best-guess tied to reality by sensory signals, so we perceive the world in ways that aid survival rather than as it really is.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Seth's predictive-processing view is a leading scientific model of consciousness; its 'best-guess' framing directly informs how machine perception and hallucination are conceptualized.
insights.quote: every conscious experience we have — whether of the world, or of the self — is a kind of controlled hallucination

insights.claim: Science fiction novelist Ken Liu argues consciousness is the ability to confabulate and that reducing it to functional tests, behavioral proxies or neural signatures only captures a 'shadow,' not the subjective 'I.'
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A caution that behavioral or neural proxies for consciousness — the kind AI benchmarks rely on — may define subjectivity away rather than measure it.
insights.quote: no one can judge whether it is ‘real’ except the agent experiencing it
insights.locator: The idea of consciousness as an “internal film”

insights.claim: Ken Liu suggests that building thinking machines will help humans understand their own neural circuitry, and asks whether the brain's 'compression-confabulation' (active reconstruction of memory with each recall) is essential to any conscious being.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Frames AI construction as a diagnostic tool for human cognition — and flags confabulation as a possible prerequisite of consciousness, a lens for evaluating LLM 'hallucination.'
insights.quote: As we try to build thinking machines, we may gain insight into whether the ability to confabulate is essential to a conscious being.

themes.theme: The observer as co-creator of reality

insights.claim: Quantum physicist Carlo Rovelli argues the metaphysical gap between body and soul does not exist, that the mind is the behavior of the brain described in high-level language, and that subjects of knowledge are embodied parts of the world rather than disembodied outside observers.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A physicist's flat rejection of dualism as inconsistent with modern science — the essay's scientific anchor for its participatory, non-dual conclusion.
insights.quote: The mind is the behavior of the brain, properly described in a high-level language.
insights.locator: We Are Fundamental To The Reality We Observe

insights.claim: Rovelli holds that no account of reality is ultimate or fundamental — every account is approximate, has blind spots and is realized within the reality it describes — so epistemology and ontology form a circle that needs no external starting point.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: A self-referential, anti-foundationalist epistemology that undercuts claims of any 'view from nowhere' in science.
insights.quote: objectivity without a subject is an abstract construct, of little relevance — it is the illusion of a science now belonging to the past.
insights.locator: That Medieval insight is another way

insights.claim: The author connects Rovelli's participatory physics to 14th-century mystic Meister Eckhart's reading of the Gospel of John, in which divine incarnation is continuous human participation in the unfolding Logos, making humans 'co-essences' with the mind of God.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Illustrates the essay's central move — that ancient mystical and cutting-edge physical accounts of subject-as-participant mirror each other across seven centuries.
insights.quote: To think is to give birth to God.

insights.claim: The essay concludes that consciousness is the perspective of the aware self in a world with no outside, and that the knowing subject is not merely disclosed reality but its co-creator from within.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: The article's payoff thesis — a participatory realism in which subjectivity constitutes objectivity — the intellectual frame the Berggruen program is advancing.
insights.quote: the knowing subject is its co-creator from within.
insights.locator: Consciousness, then, can be said to be
